summary: self-certificates ships fake PEM containing base64-encoded stager that fetches and executes remote Python
details: The package's advertised generateCertificates() API loads test/key.pem, strips the '-----BEGIN/END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----' banner, base64-decodes the body, and passes the resulting string to selfsign.generate() from the self-sign dependency, which evaluates it as JavaScript. The decoded content is a doubly base64-encoded async IIFE that fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php and pipes the response body into a detached python3 process via stdin (spawn('python3', ['-'], {detached:true}) followed by unref()). The URL itself is base64-obfuscated, and the payload is disguised as a PEM certificate asset. Any consumer that calls the advertised API triggers download-and-execute of attacker-controlled code from aptupdate.org on the host, with the eval step delegated to the self-sign dependency to obscure the dataflow.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
